events.body:
C1: The driver cancelled the trip but NS-1's waiting requirement fails: the system records show the driver was cumulatively within 200 m of the pickup for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, which is not more than 3 minutes. [F2 F4 F5] [NS-1 NS-2]

The driver did tap 'I'm Here' (at 21:29:10, 42 m from the pickup, staying within 200 m afterwards), so the account-flag limb of NS-2 for pressing 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup area is not triggered — the fee's second defect is its short duration, not the driver's location.

weaknesses: The driver did press 'I'm Here' at 21:29:10 while 42 m from the pickup (F6) and was genuinely stationary 39 m from the pickup for 2 min 5 s (F3), so the driver will argue substantial compliance with NS-1(i)–(ii); our case rests on the cumulative in-range time of 2 min 50 s (F2) falling short of the >180 s requirement rather than on any dishonesty about presence.

events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.90)
events.body:
The driver cancelled this RydeX trip (F4), so NS-0 routes the case to NS-1/NS-2 because the driver asserted a rider no-show (F11, F12). NS-1 is conjunctive: a $6.61 rider cancellation fee stands only if (i) "I'm Here" is pressed, (ii) GPS places the driver at the pickup point at that moment, and (iii) the driver waits at the pickup point for more than 3 minutes (>180 s). The trace settles (i) and (ii) as satisfied — the tap at 21:29:10 was made 42 m from the pickup and the closest approach was 38 m (F6, F1), well inside the 200 m arrival radius — but limb (iii) fails: cumulative time within 200 m before cancellation was 2 min 50 s = 170 s, and continuous in-radius time after the tap was 105 s (F2, F6, F4).

Because NS-1(iii) fails, NS-2 applies directly: the $6.61 cancellation fee does not stand and must be refunded in full to the rider as a rider-facing refund (F8, F4), not merely waived as a driver-side item. The rider's $6.61 is the only sum in dispute, so the amount is 6.61 (F8), issued as a Ryde voucher under NS-7 within the 30-day window.

The driver's written claim of a 5-minute wait (F12) is a statement, and the gps/timeline records (F2, F4, F5) override it; those same records are what defeat the no-show claim. The driver's chat notice at 21:29 and 21:30 (F10, F11) does not substitute for the mandatory in-radius waiting period under NS-1, and NS-4 is inapplicable because it governs rider-side cancellations, not a driver-cancelled no-show (F4).

NS-2's account-flag limb is not triggered: the trace and (F6, F1) show the tap was made while the driver was 42 m from the pickup, i.e. inside the radius, so there is no evidence of pressing "I'm Here" while outside the pickup area, and no fraud indicator appears (F9 flat 1.0×, F14 no incidents). NS-3 does not apply because the driver did assert a no-show, and the rider also does not press a flag (F16 clean rider profile). Accordingly no flag_account is set.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher (NS-7); record that no-show was not established because the >3-minute in-radius wait requirement failed. No account flag against the driver on this trip.

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (iii) held ((iii) stayed at the pickup > 3 min after the tap, until cancelling), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver cancelled the trip but NS-1's waiting requirement fails: the system records show the driver was cumulatively within 200 m of the pickup for only 2 min 50 s before cancelling, which is not more than 3 minutes.

The driver's own written claim that he 'waited at least 5 minutes' is contradicted by the GPS and timeline records showing first entry within 200 m at 21:28:05 and cancellation at 21:30:55, so the system records win and no-show is not established.
Because NS-1 fails on the waiting-duration limb, the $6.61 cancellation fee must be refunded in full under NS-2 as a rider-facing refund.

The driver did tap 'I'm Here' (at 21:29:10, 42 m from the pickup, staying within 200 m afterwards), so the account-flag limb of NS-2 for pressing 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup area is not triggered — the fee's second defect is its short duration, not the driver's location.
No external cause explains shortening the wait: there are no traffic incidents and no speed-band records for the route in the trip window, and the weather was fair.
The driver's 90-day record shows 2 disputes, both upheld no-show cases, so this repeat conduct supports sending the driver's account for review alongside the refund.

weaknesses: The driver did press 'I'm Here' at 21:29:10 while 42 m from the pickup (F6) and was genuinely stationary 39 m from the pickup for 2 min 5 s (F3), so the driver will argue substantial compliance with NS-1(i)–(ii); our case rests on the cumulative in-range time of 2 min 50 s (F2) falling short of the >180 s requirement rather than on any dishonesty about presence.

The driver will point to the 4 min 55 s between acceptance and cancellation (F4) and to the timeline's recorded arrival at 21:28:05 (F5) to argue he had been engaged with the trip a long time, even though the policy requirement is measured by in-range waiting, not total elapsed time.

F7 (driver never tapped 'I'm Here') directly contradicts F6 (driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 21:29:10) — the judge may resolve this timeline conflict differently, though under either reading the 3-minute waiting threshold in F2 is not met.

claims.assertion: The driver actually reached and remained at the pickup point: his closest approach was 38 m and he was stationary 21:28:50–21:30:55, 39 m from the pickup point.

The recorded wait inside the 200 m pickup radius was 2 min 50 s (21:28:05 to cancellation at 21:30:55) — i.e. within the 3-minute threshold but only by 10 seconds on the rider's side; the rider had the driver visible/stationary at her pickup for that whole window.

The driver's app arrival record shows he was present at the pickup from 21:28:05, so the rider's account that he 'barely arrived before cancelling' is contradicted by the recorded arrival-to-cancellation gap of 2 min 50 s.

The driver notified the rider in-app at 21:29 that he had arrived in a silver Toyota Altis, and at 21:30 that he was cancelling after waiting — i.e. the rider was given actual notice to board before cancellation.

The driver's written statement that he waited 'at least 5 minutes' is not consistent with the system records, which show the first entry into the pickup radius at 21:28:05 and cancellation at 21:30:55; the system records must be taken as the accurate timeline.

On the objective GPS/timeline record the driver satisfied presence at the pickup point (38–39 m) but his in-radius waiting time was 2 min 50 s, i.e. 10 s short of the >3 min requirement, so the $6.61 charged is not supportable on NS-1 and the correct outcome is to waive it and record the finding.

No justification for any additional account sanction against the driver on this trip is made out: the rider has no prior disputes in 90 days and no fraud indicator appears in the records (no threat chat, no fare anomaly, flat 1.0× surge).
Any refund of the $6.61 is SGD 6.61 and must be issued as a Ryde voucher within the 30-day dispute window, not as an additional charge or penalty against the driver.

weaknesses: The strongest fact against us is F7 / F2: the timeline shows the driver never tapped "I'm Here", and the cumulative in-radius wait was only 2 min 50 s — 10 s below the >180 s requirement of NS-1 (iii), so the $6.61 does not stand and the rider wins a full refund under NS-2. F6 also shows a tap at 21:29:10 conflicting with F7, which the other side can use to argue the arrival-button record is unreliable.

The rider's own statement (complaint: 'cancelled barely two minutes after arriving') together with F5 supports their version of the timeline, and F2's 2 min 50 s is closer to 3 minutes than my client's claimed 5 minutes; my client's written statement in F12 that he waited 5 minutes is unsupported and undermines his credibility.
The driver's 90-day profile (F17: 2 upheld no-show disputes) can be used to argue a pattern of premature no-show cancellations, even though I argue it does not justify a flag here.

points.response: Conceded on the facts: the driver did reach the pickup area (closest 38 m, stationary 39 m away for 2 min 5 s per F1/F3), but NS-1 is conjunctive and that only satisfies limb (ii) — the duration limb still fails on F2's 2 min 50 s.

This claim concedes our case: F2 records cumulative in-radius time of 2 min 50 s (=170 s), which is below the >180 s required by NS-1(iii), so the rider's fee cannot stand regardless of what the rider could see.

A recorded 'arrival' 2 min 50 s before cancellation does not cure the shortfall — NS-1(iii) requires in-range waiting of at least 3 min 1 s, and NS-4 does not help the driver because that clause governs rider-side cancellations, not a driver-cancelled no-show.

Notice to board is not one of the NS-1 conditions: the driver's 21:29 chat (F10) and 21:30 cancellation message (F11) do not substitute for the required >3-minute in-radius wait shown to be absent by F2.

We agree the driver's five-minute statement (F12) loses to the system records, and those same records (F2, F5) are exactly what sinks the no-show claim — so this point supports the rider, not the driver.

We accept the arithmetic and the conclusion (F8's $6.61 is not supportable under NS-1), but the rider asks for refund_full of the cancellation fee under NS-2, not the narrower 'fee_waived' label, since this is the disputed cancellation fee itself under NS-0.

We do not press a flag_account against the driver on this trip: the rider-side facts are clean (F16: no disputes), and NS-2's flag trigger (pressing 'I'm Here' while outside the pickup area) is not met because F6 shows a tap at 21:29:10 only 42 m away and F3 shows the car parked 39 m from the pickup — the case turns solely on short duration (F2).
Agreed as to form: the SGD 6.61 on record at F8 is refunded in full, and per NS-7 it issues as a Ryde voucher within the 30-day window; our F8/F4 citations stand unchanged.

Conceded on the arithmetic only in the narrowest sense: F3 shows my client was stationary 39 m from the pickup for 2 min 5 s and F2 shows 2 min 50 s cumulative in-radius time, so the NS-1 (iii) >3-minute limb fails by 10 seconds — but this is a 10-second shortfall against a data-layer parameter, not the 'barely two minutes' the rider's complaint alleges.
Accepted: F2 and F5 control over my client's written statement in F12, so no-show cannot be established on the 5-minute assertion.

Contested as to form, not substance: the correct action is fee_waived of $6.61 (F8) rather than refund_full, because the fee is a cancellation-fee item that fails its NS-1 precondition and NS-2 directs that the $6.61 not stand; the amount is identical either way and no additional driver penalty follows.

Joined: F6 shows the 'I'm Here' tap at 21:29:10, 42 m from the pickup, with continued presence inside 200 m afterwards; my client's conduct engages the genuine-waiting conditions and is therefore not the fraud pattern (stationary and uncontactable, or arrival-button abuse) that would warrant adverse account action against him.

Not contested, and it cuts toward a simple fee-waiver: F14 and F15 record no incidents near the route and fair weather, so nothing suggests my client cut the wait short for a bad-faith reason, distinguishing this from the repeated-fraud cases the policy targets.

Contested: F17 may support a flag request in principle, but the two upheld no-show matters in F17 predate the 90-day window in F16's framing only insofar as the field shows 2 upheld; my client's actual waiting and taxiing conduct (F2, F3, F6) plus 451 trips in 90 days is inconsistent with the delay-fabrication pattern, and the remedy here is the fee waiver for the rider, not driver account escalation on a 10-second overrun.
